project.name: NexusAI
project.full_name: NexusAI - Enterprise Knowledge & AI Intelligence Platform
project.description: A multi-user enterprise knowledge management platform that allows organizations to upload, organize, search, and retrieve internal documents using AI-powered Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG).
project.vision: To provide organizations with a centralized, secure, and intelligent knowledge platform that transforms unstructured documents into accessible and actionable information.

primary.description: Provide a single platform for storing and managing internal organizational documents.
Allow users to ask natural language questions and retrieve relevant information from uploaded documents.
Reduce the time required to find information in large collections of documents.
Implement authentication, role-based access control, and document-level permissions.
Provide analytics about document usage, AI interactions, user activity, and system performance.

success_metrics.measurement: Successful document processing divided by total valid upload attempts.
Successfully completed AI responses divided by total valid questions.
Responses containing valid document references divided by responses requiring citations.

problems.title: Scattered organizational documents
problems.description: Organizational information is distributed across multiple files and storage locations, making it difficult to manage.

problems.title: Time-consuming information retrieval
problems.description: Employees must manually search through lengthy documents to find specific information.

problems.title: Limited contextual search
problems.description: Traditional keyword search cannot always understand the context or intent behind a user's question.

problems.title: Uncontrolled information access
problems.description: Organizations need a way to ensure users can only retrieve information they are authorized to access.

problems.title: Lack of usage visibility
problems.description: Administrators need insights into document usage, user activity, and AI system performance.

problem_statement.proposed_solution: NexusAI combines document management, semantic search, Retrieval Augmented Generation, role-based authorization, and analytics into one integrated platform.

personas.name: System Administrator
personas.description: Responsible for managing the organization, users, roles, permissions, and system configuration.

personas.name: Knowledge Manager
personas.description: Responsible for managing organizational knowledge and maintaining document collections.

personas.name: Employee
personas.description: An organization member who uses AI to search and retrieve information from authorized documents.

roles.name: MANAGER
roles.description: Manages knowledge resources and authorized document collections.

roles.name: EMPLOYEE
roles.description: Uses authorized knowledge resources and AI chat functionality.

authorization_rules: Every authenticated user must belong to an organization.
Every organization must have isolated data access.
Users must not access resources belonging to another organization.
Employees can only retrieve documents they are authorized to access.
Document permissions must be validated before retrieving vector search results.
Users can only view their own conversations unless an explicitly authorized administrative feature is implemented.
Administrators can manage users and organization-level configurations.
Every protected backend endpoint must validate authentication and authorization.

frontend.version_policy: Use a stable release compatible with the selected dependencies.

system_architecture.architecture_style: Modular monolith with separated frontend, backend, and worker services.

document_upload: User uploads a document through Next.js.
Frontend sends the document to the FastAPI backend.
Backend validates the file, user permissions, and organization.
Original file is stored in object storage.
Document metadata and processing status are saved in PostgreSQL.
A background processing job is created.
Worker extracts and normalizes document text.
Vectors and metadata are stored in Qdrant.
ai_question: User submits a question through the chat interface.
Backend validates JWT and organization membership.
Backend checks access permissions for the requested knowledge scope.
Qdrant retrieves relevant authorized document chunks.
Backend prepares the context and source references.
Context and question are sent to the configured LLM.
Backend validates and stores the answer and source references.
Frontend displays the response and citations.

authentication.name: User Login
authentication.description: Users can log in using email and password.
acceptance_criteria: Valid credentials allow access.
Invalid credentials return a clear error.
Passwords are never stored in plaintext.
Successful login issues a secure authentication token.

authentication.name: User Logout
authentication.description: Users can terminate their authenticated session.
acceptance_criteria: User can log out from the application.
Protected pages are inaccessible after logout.
Authentication state is cleared securely.

authentication.name: User Management
authentication.description: Administrators can create, update, deactivate, and manage organization users.
acceptance_criteria: Only administrators can manage organization members.
Each user has an assigned role.
User email must be unique within the system.
Deactivated users cannot access protected services.

authentication.name: Role-Based Access Control
authentication.description: System permissions are enforced based on user roles and resource permissions.
acceptance_criteria: Unauthorized actions return HTTP 403.
Unauthenticated requests return HTTP 401.
Frontend navigation reflects user permissions.
Backend independently validates all protected actions.

dashboard.name: Overview Dashboard
dashboard.description: Display relevant organization and knowledge statistics.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard displays data from authorized organization scope.
Statistics are calculated from backend data.
Loading, empty, and error states are supported.

document_management.name: Upload Documents
document_management.description: Users with permission can upload organizational documents.

initial_constraints.duplicate_handling: Prevent duplicate files within the same organization using file checksum.

acceptance_criteria: Supported file types are accepted.
Unsupported file types are rejected.
Maximum file size is enforced.
Upload progress is displayed.
Uploaded documents receive a processing status.
Invalid uploads return meaningful errors.

document_management.name: Document Listing
document_management.description: Display documents available to the authenticated user.
acceptance_criteria: Users only see documents they are authorized to access.
Search and filtering work together.
Pagination returns consistent results.

document_management.name: Document Details
document_management.description: Display detailed information about a selected document.

document_management.name: Delete Documents
document_management.description: Authorized users can delete documents and their indexed content.
acceptance_criteria: Deletion requires confirmation.
Document metadata is removed or soft-deleted according to retention policy.
Associated vector chunks are deleted or made inaccessible.
Original files are removed according to the configured storage lifecycle.
Deletion is recorded in audit logs.

document_management.name: Document Processing Status
document_management.description: Track document ingestion and indexing progress.
acceptance_criteria: Status updates are persisted.
Failed documents display an error reason.
Failed processing can be retried by authorized users.

collections.name: Collection Management
collections.description: Organize documents into logical knowledge collections.
acceptance_criteria: Collections belong to an organization.
Documents can be associated with collections.
Users only see authorized collections.
Deleting a collection does not silently delete its documents.

ai_chat.name: AI Knowledge Assistant
ai_chat.description: Users can ask natural language questions about authorized organizational documents.
acceptance_criteria: Questions are processed using authorized knowledge only.
Responses are grounded in retrieved context.
Relevant sources are displayed.
Users receive an appropriate response when no relevant information is found.
AI provider failures are handled gracefully.
Each conversation belongs to its creator and organization.

ai_chat.name: Source Citations
ai_chat.description: Display document references used to generate AI responses.
acceptance_criteria: Every displayed citation references an existing authorized document.
Page numbers are displayed only when available.
Users cannot open documents they are not authorized to access.

ai_chat.name: Conversation History
ai_chat.description: Allow users to view and manage their previous conversations.

ai_chat.name: Contextual Conversation Memory
ai_chat.description: Maintain relevant conversation context for follow-up questions.
acceptance_criteria: Recent conversation context is included within configured limits.
Context is isolated by user and conversation.
Memory does not bypass document permissions.

ai_chat.name: Feedback
ai_chat.description: Allow users to rate AI responses.
acceptance_criteria: Feedback is associated with a specific AI message.
Feedback can be reviewed by authorized administrators.

analytics.name: Usage Analytics
acceptance_criteria: Analytics respect organization boundaries.
Time range filters are available.
Charts display backend-derived data.

analytics.name: Activity Monitoring
analytics.description: Display important user and system activities.

stages.name: Text Extraction
stages.description: Extract textual content from supported file formats.

stages.name: Text Chunking
stages.description: Divide extracted text into smaller semantic units.

stages.name: Embedding Generation
stages.description: Convert document chunks into vector embeddings.

stages.name: Vector Indexing
stages.description: Store vectors and metadata in Qdrant.

stages.name: Query Processing
stages.description: Prepare a user question for semantic retrieval.

stages.name: Retrieval
stages.description: Retrieve relevant authorized chunks from Qdrant.

stages.name: Context Construction
stages.description: Prepare retrieved information for LLM generation.

stages.name: LLM Generation
stages.description: Generate an answer based on retrieved context.
rules: Use retrieved documents as the primary knowledge source.
Clearly indicate when available information is insufficient.

stages.name: Response Persistence
stages.description: Store generated responses and their citations.

security_requirements: Apply access filters before returning vector search results.
Validate document access using backend authorization rules.
Revalidate permissions when displaying source documents.
Keep LLM API keys on the backend.

entities.description: Stores source citations for assistant messages.
Stores user feedback for AI responses.

relationships: One collection can contain many documents.
One document can have many chunks.
One document can have many permission records.
One user can create many conversations.
One conversation can contain many messages.
One assistant message can reference many document chunks.
One organization can have many audit logs.
database_constraints: Use foreign keys for relational integrity.
Add indexes for frequently queried organization_id fields.
Add indexes for document status and creation timestamps.
Use unique constraints for organization slugs and user emails.
Use transactions for multi-step document lifecycle operations.
Use soft deletion where required by retention policy.

routes.description: Get current user profile and permissions.
Deactivate or delete a user according to policy.
Submit a question and generate an AI response.
Submit feedback for an AI response.

http_status_codes.204: Successful request with no response body.

public.name: Forgot Password
public.description: Password recovery page, enabled when email delivery is configured.

performance.requirement: Dashboard initial content should load within 3 seconds under the agreed test environment.
Standard API requests should target a response time below 500ms at the 95th percentile, excluding external AI calls and large file operations.
Document processing must run asynchronously for potentially long-running operations.

security.requirement: Hash passwords using a secure password hashing algorithm.
Protect authentication tokens and use secure cookie settings where applicable.
Prevent SQL injection and common web application vulnerabilities.
Apply rate limiting to authentication, upload, and AI chat endpoints.
Never expose API keys or secrets in frontend code.
Enforce organization isolation and document-level authorization.

reliability.requirement: External AI provider failures must not crash the application.
Failed document jobs must be observable and retryable.
Critical document operations must maintain consistency between PostgreSQL, object storage, and Qdrant.

maintainability.requirement: Use automated tests for critical business logic.
Use environment variables for environment-specific configuration.

frontend: Display clear and actionable error messages.
Show loading states during asynchronous operations.
Display empty states when no data is available.
backend: Avoid exposing internal stack traces to clients.

security_rules: Never commit environment files containing secrets.
Only expose explicitly public variables to the frontend.
Use separate credentials for development and production.

architecture: Follow the architecture defined in this PRD.
Keep frontend and backend responsibilities separated.
Use service and repository layers for backend business logic and data access.
Keep business logic out of presentation components.
Use database migrations for schema changes.
coding_standards: Write clear function and variable names.
ai_coding_agent_rules: Read PRD.json before implementing any feature.
Inspect the existing project structure before modifying files.
Do not rewrite the entire application when fixing a small issue.
Do not change the selected technology stack without explicit approval.
Do not create duplicate components or services.
Do not invent backend endpoints that are not documented.
Keep API contracts consistent between frontend and backend.
Use mock data only during the frontend development phase.
Replace mock data with real API integration in the appropriate phase.
Run relevant tests after making changes.
Report modified files and implementation status after each task.

project_constraints: The initial version is a web application, not a native mobile application.
The initial architecture is a modular monolith.
PostgreSQL is the primary relational database.
Next.js and TypeScript are used for the frontend.
AI provider integrations must be configurable.
All AI retrieval operations must enforce document authorization.
The initial development process prioritizes a complete frontend UI before full backend integration.
Advanced AI orchestration is deferred until the core RAG pipeline works reliably.
definition_of_done: The feature satisfies its acceptance criteria.
The implementation follows the approved architecture.
Authorization checks are implemented where required.
Loading, empty, success, and error states are handled.
API documentation is updated when endpoints change.
The feature works with the integrated application.
